lines: Three plates. Three stones. Somewhere over your head a counterweight
finds out it is heavier than the thing holding it, and gives up.
The cage comes down the shaft behind the two hands, and they step aside.
Cage doesn't run till the counterweight's set. Three plates, three stones.
You can't pull them, only push. So think about which side you want to be on.
And if you wedge one somewhere stupid, walk out and walk back in.
They go home. Everything in here goes home eventually.
That's the joke. It is not a very good joke. We tell it a lot.
Cage is down. Mind the gap at the bottom, it's wider than it looks.
And keep to the road round the water. The water is not a road.
This gallery worked for sixty years and the Hall has had it for twelve.
Everything in it still does the job it always did. That's her doing.
She wouldn't let them take the gear out. Said a Hall ought to be somewhere real.
